slides.title: The legal move
slides.subtitle: Fiduccia–Mattheyses refinement · single moves and the balance window
slides.byline: Learning Clustering · original author stephQ-lab (Issue #7 attachment)
slides.transcript: This module covers FM refinement: move one node at a time, with a balance window limiting the side sizes. Gains, locks, trials and the best prefix are the same as in KL; the key difference is that the largest gain is compared only among legal candidates.

slides.title: The problem, and how it differs from KL
bullets: Input: a graph (or a multi-pin netlist), an initial bisection, maxDiff
Move: one node at a time
Legal: after the move both sides are nonempty and |n₀ − n₁| ≤ maxDiff
Output: the trial moves, cumulative gains, the best prefix, the accepted bisection
Review: gain, lock, trial and best prefix are as in Module 07
slides.transcript: FM’s input is a graph, an initial bisection and a balance parameter. Each step moves one node; after the move both sides must be nonempty and the size difference at most maxDiff. Gains, locks, trials and the best prefix mean the same as in the last module.

slides.title: The largest may not be allowed to move
bullets: Seed AE | BCD, maxDiff = 1: only 2:3 or 3:2
A and E gain +6, but sit on the left, which has 2 nodes
Moving either leaves 1 : 4: not legal

bullets.text: Legal candidates B +1, C −4, D +3 → choose D

slides.transcript: On the seed, A and E both gain 6, but they are on the left, which has only two nodes; moving either makes it 1 to 4, which breaks the balance. The largest gain among the legal candidates is D’s, plus 3.

slides.title: Splitting a gain: FS and TE
bullets: FS: v is a net’s only pin on its side → +w
TE: a net has no pin on the target side → −w
D: FS = D–E (5), TE = C–D (2), gain 3
On 2-pin edges: FS − TE = external − internal
slides.transcript: A gain splits into two parts. FS: the node is a net’s only pin on its side, so after the move the net is no longer cut, plus w. TE: a net has no pin on the target side, so after the move it becomes cut, minus w. D’s gain is 5 minus 2, which is 3.

slides.title: One full pass
bullets: D +3 (cut 9) → the left has 3 nodes, and A becomes legal
A +6 (cut 3)
Then C −2, E −6, B −1: tried anyway
The cut runs 12, 9, 3, 5, 11, 12
slides.transcript: Pass 1: D, plus 3, cut 9; now the left has three nodes, A becomes legal, plus 6, cut 3. Every gain after that is negative; C, E and B are tried in turn, and the cut ends back at 12.

slides.title: The best prefix and roll-back
bullets: Cumulative gains 3, 9, 7, 1, 0
k* = 2: apply only D and A
Accept ABC | DE, cut 3
The trials’ end at cut 12 is discarded; pass 2’s prefix is empty, so stop
slides.transcript: The cumulative gains are 3, 9, 7, 1 and 0; the largest is the first two steps. Back at the start, do only D and A, and accept ABC versus DE, cut 3. Pass 2’s best prefix is empty, and the algorithm stops.

slides.title: Auditing the attachment’s hillclimb claim
bullets: The text: initial cut 9, legal gains all ≤ 0, final 4
From the attachment’s data: initial cut 18
E is legal, with gain +10
Pass 1’s best 8 = the exhaustive balanced optimum 8

bullets.text: Text and data disagree: a regression test only, not teaching material

slides.transcript: The original attachment has a case about climbing out with negative gains; we check it with its own data. The initial cut is 18, not 9; E’s move is legal, with gain plus 10; pass 1’s best and the exhaustive optimum are both 8, not 4. So it cannot serve as the example, and this course keeps it only as a regression test.

slides.title: The replacement: negative first, then positive
bullets: 6 nodes, seed ADE | BCF, maxDiff = 2, cut 6
At the start every legal gain ≤ 0: hill climbing stops at 6
FM: A −1, B −1 (cut 8), then E +4 (cut 4)
Keep 3 steps: cut 4 = the exhaustive balanced optimum
Found by a seeded search, verified exhaustively in the tests
slides.transcript: This course’s replacement example: at the start every legal move has gain at most 0, so moving only on positive gains stops at cut 6. FM moves A and B one step each, the cut rises to 8, and then E’s gain becomes plus 4, cut 4 after the move. Keeping the first three steps gives exactly the balanced optimum found by exhaustive search.

slides.title: Buckets, complexity and multi-pin nets
bullets: The paper: bucket lists + a max-gain pointer → O(P) per pass
This course: gains update incrementally, but selection still scans: not O(P)
Multi-pin nets: decide FS/TE by counting pins per side
net{A,B,C,D}, D on the right: A gains 0, D +3; a clique would give −1
The attachment’s “hypergraph” case has only 2-pin edges
slides.transcript: The paper reaches linear time with bucket lists and a max-gain pointer. This course updates gains incrementally, but still scans to choose, so it cannot be called linear time. A real multi-pin net is decided by counting pins: in the example A’s gain is 0, while splitting it into a clique and counting edges gives minus 1.

slides.title: The pseudocode, line by line
bullets: Line 2: compute gains by counting per net (gain)
Lines 3–4: take the largest among legal candidates only (legal_moves)
Lines 5–6: trial, lock, incremental update
Lines 7–8: best prefix and roll-back; line 9: stop on the empty prefix
slides.transcript: Line 2 of the pseudocode computes gains by counting per net; lines 3 and 4 take the largest among legal candidates only; lines 5 and 6 make the trial, lock and update incrementally; lines 7 and 8 roll back to the best prefix; on the empty prefix it stops.

slides.title: Common mistakes
bullets: Picking the largest gain outright (ignoring balance)
Copying the attachment’s hillclimb claim
Taking “buckets drawn” for “linear time implemented”
Calling a 2-pin example a hypergraph
Thinking count balance is area balance
slides.transcript: Common mistakes: picking the largest gain without looking at the balance; copying an unverified example; taking a bucket display for a linear-time implementation; calling a 2-pin example a hypergraph; and taking count balance for area balance.

slides.title: Summary
lines: Filter for legality, then take the largest; try negative gains too; accept only the best prefix.
Verify examples by independent computation; buckets on screen are not a linear-time implementation.
Next module: the goal changes from the cut to delay, and nodes may be copied.
slides.transcript: In summary: filter for legality first, then take the largest; try negative gains too, and accept only the best prefix. Examples must be verified by independent computation, and buckets on screen are not a linear-time implementation. The next module changes the goal from the cut to delay, and allows nodes to be copied.
